puzzles.teaser: A man describes his daughters: 'They are all blonde, but two; all brunette, but two; and all redheaded, but two.' How many daughters does he have?
puzzles.answer: Three (one blonde, one brunette, and one redhead).

puzzles.teaser: You see a boat filled with people. It has not capsized, but when you look again, not a single person is on the boat. How?
puzzles.answer: All the people on the boat were married!

puzzles.teaser: Two mothers and two daughters went out for lunch, but they only ordered three meals and everyone had one. How?
puzzles.answer: It was a grandmother, her daughter, and her granddaughter.

puzzles.teaser: A barrel of water weighs 50 pounds. What can you add to it to make it weigh 35 pounds?
What five-letter word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?
I have four legs in the morning, two legs at noon, and three legs in the evening. What am I?
puzzles.answer: A human (crawling as a baby, walking as an adult, using a cane as an elder).

puzzles.teaser: A man was driving a black car with no headlights down a road with no streetlights. A black cat ran across the road, but he stopped in time. How did he see it?
What number comes next in the sequence: 1, 11, 21, 1211, 111221...?
If a red house is made of red bricks and a blue house is made of blue bricks, what is a greenhouse made of?
What day comes two days after the day before yesterday?
A farmer has 17 sheep and all but 9 die. How many sheep are left?
If you are running in a race and you pass the person in second place, what place are you in?
A man leaves home, turns left three times, and returns home to find two men wearing masks waiting for him. Who are they?
puzzles.answer: The catcher and the umpire (it's a game of baseball).

puzzles.teaser: What can you hold in your right hand, but never in your left hand?
There are three apples in a basket and you take away two. How many apples do you have?
A doctor and a bus driver are both in love with the same woman, Sarah. The bus driver had to go on a long trip for 7 days. Before he left, he gave Sarah 7 apples. Why?
puzzles.answer: An apple a day keeps the doctor away!

puzzles.teaser: What turns everything around, but does not move?
Before Mount Everest was discovered, what was the highest mountain in the world?
puzzles.answer: Mount Everest (it was still the highest, just not discovered yet).

puzzles.teaser: How many times can you subtract 10 from 100?
puzzles.answer: Only once. After that, you are subtracting from 90.

puzzles.teaser: A man drops his hat in a deep well. How does he get it out?
What breaks on the water but never on the land?
If a rooster lays an egg on the peak of a barn roof, which side does it roll down?
What has 88 keys, but cannot open a single door?
What gets wetter the more it dries?
What can travel all around the world while remaining in the exact same corner?
I have cities, but no houses. I have mountains, but no trees. I have water, but no fish. What am I?
What belongs to you, but everyone else uses it far more than you do?
What is light as a feather, yet even the world's strongest person cannot hold it for more than 5 minutes?
What builds up castles, tears down mountains, blinds some men, and helps others see?
The person who makes it doesn't want it. The person who buys it doesn't use it. The person who uses it doesn't know it. What is it?
What has a head and a tail, but no body?
What word in the dictionary is always spelled incorrectly?
What has four fingers and a thumb, but is not alive?
A man pushes his car to a hotel and tells the owner he's bankrupt. Why?
What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
If you have me, you want to share me. If you share me, you haven't got me. What am I?
What can fill a room without taking up any physical space?
If 5 cats can catch 5 mice in 5 minutes, how many cats does it take to catch 100 mice in 100 minutes?
A plane crashes on the border of the United States and Canada. Where do they bury the survivors?
What has a neck but no head?
Which weighs more: a pound of feathers or a pound of bricks?
puzzles.answer: Neither—they both weigh exactly one pound.

puzzles.teaser: I am an odd number. Take away a letter and I become even. What number am I?
What has to be broken before you can use it?
I'm tall when I'm young, and I'm short when I'm old. What am I?
What goes up but never comes down?
What can you break, even if you never pick it up or touch it?
What goes through cities and fields, but never moves?
What has one eye, but cannot see anything?
What has hands, but cannot clap?
What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
There is a one-story house where everything inside is yellow. What color are the stairs?
puzzles.answer: There are no stairs (it's a one-story house).

puzzles.teaser: What is so fragile that saying its name breaks it?
What can you catch, but never throw?
What runs all around a backyard, yet never moves?
If a brother, his sister, and their dog weren't under an umbrella, why didn't they get wet?
What has many legs, but cannot walk?
What has teeth, but cannot bite?
Where does today come before yesterday?
What has a thumb, but no fingers?
What goes up and down, but stays in the same place?
What has a spine, but no bones?
What loses its head in the morning, but gets it back at night?
What has a heart that doesn't beat?
puzzles.answer: An artichoke (or a deck of cards).

puzzles.teaser: What begins with T, ends with T, and has T in it?
What kind of coat is best put on wet?
What has a bed but never sleeps, and runs but never walks?
If two's a company, and three's a crowd, what are four and five?
What umbrella does a king use when it rains?
What passes in front of the sun without casting a shadow?
What gets sharper the more you use it?
What four-letter word can be written forward, backward, or upside down and still be read left to right?
What asks no questions, but requires many answers?
What has branches, but no fruit, trunk, or leaves?
What never asks questions, but is answered all the time?
What has words, but never speaks?
What flies without wings?
What has thousands of needles, but cannot sew?
I am not alive, but I grow; I don't have lungs, but I need air; I don't have a mouth, but water kills me. What am I?
What travels faster: heat or cold?
puzzles.answer: Heat, because you can easily catch a cold!

puzzles.teaser: What is black when you buy it, red when you use it, and gray when you throw it away?
What can you throw out when you want to use it, and pull back in when you are done?
What has 13 hearts, but no other organs?
What key cannot open any door?
puzzles.answer: A donkey (or a piano key / monkey / turkey).

puzzles.teaser: You are in a dark room with a candle, a wood stove, and a gas lamp. You only have one match. What do you light first?
A man dies of old age on his 25th birthday. How is this possible?
puzzles.answer: He was born on February 29th (a leap year).

puzzles.teaser: How can a door be non-existent?
What double-digit number multiplied by itself equals the sum of its digits multiplied by 18?
Two fathers and two sons go fishing. They each catch one fish, but bring home 3 fish in total. How?
puzzles.answer: There are only 3 people: a grandfather, his son, and his grandson.

puzzles.teaser: A thief enters a shop and steals a $100 bill. He then buys $70 worth of goods using the $100 bill. The shopkeeper gives him $30 change. How much money did the store lose?
What side of a turkey has the most feathers?
How many months have 28 days?
If there are 6 apples and you take away 4, how many do you have?
A man is looking at a photograph of someone. His friend asks who it is. He replies: 'Brothers and sisters I have none, but that man's father is my father's son.' Who is in the photo?
What 5-letter word can be read the same upside down and upside right?
What can you hold without ever touching it with your hands?
puzzles.answer: Your breath (or a conversation / a grudge).

puzzles.teaser: Where can you find roads without cars, forests without trees, and cities without houses?
What kind of room has no walls, doors, or windows?
What runs, but never walks; murmurs, but never talks; has a bed, but never sleeps?
What invention lets you look right through a wall?
What moves faster than the speed of light?
